::: {#exr-prac-gauss-iid-lik}
#### Gaussian log-likelihood (adapted from @kleinbaum2014applied, Chapter 5)

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n \siid \Normal(\mu, \sigma^2)$.

**(a)** Write the likelihood $\Lik(\mu, \sigma^2; \vx)$
for the observed data $\vx = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)$.

**(b)** Write the log-likelihood $\ell(\mu, \sigma^2; \vx)$.
Show that it can be written as

$$
\ell(\mu, \sigma^2; \vx)
= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\sigma^2}
  - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2.
$$

**(c)** Derive the MLE $\hat\mu_{ML}$ and $\hat\sigma^2_{ML}$.
:::

:::{#sol-prac-gauss-iid-lik}

**(a)**

$$
\ba
\Lik(\mu, \sigma^2; \vx)
&= \prod_{i=1}^n (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/2}
  \expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}
&& \text{(likelihood of an $\iid$ sample)}
\\
&= \paren{\prod_{i=1}^n (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-1/2}}
  \paren{\prod_{i=1}^n \expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}}
&& \text{(regroup the factors of the product)}
\\
&= (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-n/2}
  \prod_{i=1}^n \expf{-\frac{(x_i - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}
&& \text{(product of $n$ copies of a power)}
\\
&= (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-n/2}
  \expf{\sum_{i=1}^n -\frac{(x_i - \mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}}
&& \text{(product of exponentials)}
\\
&= (2\pi\sigma^2)^{-n/2}
  \expf{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i-\mu)^2}
&& \text{(factor the constant out of the sum)}
\ea
$$

**(b)**

$$
\ba
\ell(\mu, \sigma^2; \vx)
&= \logf{\Lik(\mu, \sigma^2; \vx)}
&& \text{(definition of the log-likelihood)}
\\
&= \logf{(2\pi\sigma^2)^{-n/2}
  \expf{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i-\mu)^2}}
&& \text{(likelihood from (a))}
\\
&= \logf{(2\pi\sigma^2)^{-n/2}}
  + \logf{\expf{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i-\mu)^2}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\sigma^2}
  + \logf{\expf{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i-\mu)^2}}
&& \text{(log of a power)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\sigma^2}
   - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{($\logt$ undoes $\expt$)}
\ea
$$

**(c)**

**Deriving $\hat\mu_{ML}$:**

$$
\ba
\deriv{\mu}\ell
&= \deriv{\mu}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\sigma^2}
   - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(log-likelihood from (b))}
\\
&= \deriv{\mu}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\sigma^2}}
   + \deriv{\mu}\sb{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= 0 + \deriv{\mu}\sb{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\\
&= \deriv{\mu}\sb{-\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\deriv{\mu}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n \deriv{\mu}(x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(derivative of a sum is the sum of derivatives)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n 2(x_i - \mu)\deriv{\mu}(x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(chain rule, outer function $u^2$)}
\ea
$$

The inner derivative is:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\mu}(x_i - \mu)
&= \deriv{\mu} x_i - \deriv{\mu} \mu
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= 0 - \deriv{\mu} \mu
&& \text{($x_i$ does not depend on $\mu$)}
\\
&= 0 - 1
&& \text{(derivative of $\mu$ with respect to itself)}
\\
&= -1
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

Substituting the inner derivative back in:

$$
\ba
\deriv{\mu}\ell
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n 2(x_i - \mu) \cdot (-1)
&& \text{(inner derivative is $-1$)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n -2(x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= -\frac{1}{2\sigma^2} \cdot (-2) \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(factor the constant $-2$ out of the sum)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)
&& \text{(multiply the constants)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i - \sum_{i=1}^n \mu}
&& \text{(split the sum)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{\sigma^2}\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i - n\mu}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\mu$)}
\ea
$$

Setting this to zero: $\hat\mu_{ML} = \bar{x} \eqdef \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i$.

**Deriving $\hat\sigma^2_{ML}$:**

$$
\ba
\deriv{\sigma^2}\ell
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi\sigma^2}
   - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(log-likelihood from (b))}
\\
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\paren{\logf{2\pi} + \logf{\sigma^2}}
   - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}
   - \frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(distribute $-\tfrac{n}{2}$)}
\\
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi} - \frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}
   - \frac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(write $\tfrac{1}{2\sigma^2}$ as $\tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}$)}
\\
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{2\pi}}
   + \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}}
   + \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= 0 + \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}}
   + \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\\
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}}
   + \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\\
&= \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{n}{2}\logf{\sigma^2}}
   + \deriv{\sigma^2}\sb{-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 (\sigma^2)^{-1}}
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}\deriv{\sigma^2}\logf{\sigma^2}
   - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \deriv{\sigma^2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}
   - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \deriv{\sigma^2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}
&& \text{(derivative of $\log$)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}
   - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 \paren{-(\sigma^2)^{-2}}
&& \text{(power rule)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}
   + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2 (\sigma^2)^{-2}
&& \text{(multiply)}
\\
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}
   + \frac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}
\ea
$$

Setting this to zero and solving:

$$
\ba
0
&= -\frac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1} + \frac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(set the derivative to zero)}
\\
\frac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}
&= \frac{1}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-2}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(add $\tfrac{n}{2}(\sigma^2)^{-1}$ to both sides)}
\\
n(\sigma^2)^{-1}(\sigma^2)^2
&= (\sigma^2)^{-2}(\sigma^2)^2\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $2(\sigma^2)^2$)}
\\
n\sigma^2
&= (\sigma^2)^{-2}(\sigma^2)^2\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{($(\sigma^2)^{-1}(\sigma^2)^2 = \sigma^2$)}
\\
n\sigma^2
&= \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{($(\sigma^2)^{-2}(\sigma^2)^2 = 1$)}
\\
\sigma^2
&= \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \mu)^2
&& \text{(divide both sides by $n$)}
\ea
$$

Substituting $\hat\mu_{ML} = \bar{x}$:

$$
\hat\sigma^2_{ML} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar{x})^2
$$

Note: this maximum likelihood estimator is a biased estimator of $\sigma^2$;
the unbiased sample variance divides by $n-1$.

:::
